texts.preamble: Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others on 12 June, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt Justice P. Sree Sudha Writ Petition No.43849 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: Petitioner, who is friend of the detenue i.e., Mr Goudu Jitendra @ Narsima @Mohan@Varun filed the present Writ Petition. 3. Perusal of record would reveal that two criminal cases were registered against the detenue i.e., Cr.No.288 of 2022 pending on the file of Jagathgirigutta Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 370 (A)(2) of IPC and Sections 3,4,5 and 6 of PIT Act and Cr.No.628 of 2022 pending on the file of Kukatpally Police Stattion for the offences punishable under Section 370(A)(2) IPC and Sections 3,4 and 5 of PIT Act. In both crimes detenue released on 26.05.2022 and 19.09.2022 itself respectively. In both the bail orders conditions were imposed. Even then, 2nd respondent has invoked the procedure laid down under Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (For short, 'the Act') detained the detenue in Central Prison, Cherlapally, Medchal-Malkarjgir District on 25.11.2022. The said detention order dated 25.11.2022 was confirmed by 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.81, dated 12.01.2023. 4. Perusal of record would reveal that though the bail was granted to the detenue in first crime i.e., Cr.No.288 of 2022 on 26.05.2022, the respondent authorities have not filed any cancellation of the bail application in the said crime on the ground that detenue herein repeated the very same offences involving in Cr.No.628 of 2022. It is also relevant to note that though the detenue was released on Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24044968/ 1 19.09.2022 in the second crime, the detention order was passed on 25.11.2022.
texts.arguments: 5. In Banka Sneha Sheela v. State of Telangana1 Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere apprehension of breach of law and order cannot be a ground to invoke the harsh provisions of preventive detention. 7. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar2, the Hon'ble Supreme Court explained the phrase 'habitual criminal' as follows: "12. A person is habitual criminal who by force of-habit or inward disposition, inherent or latent in him, has grown accustomed to lead a life of crime. It is the force of habit inherent or latent in an individual with a criminal instinct, (1984) 3 SCC 14. with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him dangerous to the society in general. 9. In the similar circumstances, this Court vide order dated 29.04.2022 in W.P.No.3844 of 2022, wherein two crimes were registered against the detenue for the offences punishable under Sections Gunaganti Krishna vs The State Of Telangana And 2Others on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24044968/ 2 370 (A)(2) IPC and 354 of IPC, [LEAKAGE_MASK] the detention order by declaring it as illegal. 10. Vide order dated 30.07.2020 in K. Damla vs. the State of Telangana in W.P.No.7132 of 2020, a Division Bench of this Court held that detention order issued after 5 months of the involvement of the detenue therein is illegal. This Court and Hon'ble Apex Court, time again categorically held that provisions of the Act, 1986 have to be invoked in the rarest of the rare cases in preventing a person from committing the similar offences to prevent the public order but not law and order.
